messages.subject: stratification & global density estimate
parts:
Dear all
I have done a survey for dorcas gazelles in south Sinai. I have
tow strata in my survey. I am using distance 4 beta 3. The program
reports different global densities
If the density is calculated globaly it is 389 CV 31.9.
If density is calculated globaly as the mean of the density of the
two strata weighed by their respective area it 254.25 32.9.

I would like to use z-test to compare if there is significant difference
between the two estimates. Unfortunately Distanse doesn't report
SE for the density estimate in case2, Is there any possible was
to get it from distance or calculate it manually?
I would appreciate any help.

Husam El Alqamy

messages.subject: Re: stratification & global density estimate
parts:
> > I have done a survey for dorcas gazelles in south Sinai. I have
> > tow strata in my survey. I am using distance 4 beta 3. The program
> > reports different global densities
> > If the density is calculated globaly it is 389 CV 31.9.
> > If density is calculated globaly as the mean of the density of the
> > two strata weighed by their respective area it 254.25 32.9.
> >
> > I would like to use z-test to compare if there is significant difference
> > between the two estimates. Unfortunately Distanse doesn't report
> > SE for the density estimate in case2, Is there any possible was
> > to get it from distance or calculate it manually?
> > I would appreciate any help.

Husam, the cv is simply se/estimate, so you can easily obtain it from the
results. However, your 2 estimates are not independent, so the z-test is
not valid. If the design was in two strata, the analysis should be
stratified - at least for encounter rate. Otherwise, bias in your density
estimate will occur, unless either effort per unit area was the same in
both strata, or density was the same in both strata.

Steve
